content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_12/projects/simgate-modular-routing/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — simgate-modular-routing\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR short paper, 4 pages + references)\\n- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings\\n- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026 (11 days remaining)\\n\\n## Core Insight\\n\\nLLM agents on rule-governed environments face catastrophic failures from hallucinated state transitions. Deterministic external computation (environment simulators, code interpreters) eliminates these failures — but what exactly does routing learn? We introduce episode-level counterfactual analysis (per-step oracle labeling degenerates to 98% ties in sparse-reward settings) and discover that **death avoidance accounts for ~90% of routing signal** on ScienceWorld (Δ_full=+29.60, Δ_no_death=+2.84, death fraction=90.41%; Pearson r=0.9698, p=8.12e-07 across 11 task types / 245 episodes). Non-death performance is approximately equal between modalities, with one notable exception: find-non-living-thing (zero deaths) shows Δ=+9.58 from non-death mechanisms. The contribution is the empirical finding (death avoidance dominance) + the diagnostic methodology (episode-level counterfactual labeling), not the router architecture itself.\\n\\n## Core Claims (2 claims for short paper)\\n\\n**C1 (Death avoidance dominates routing signal)**: On ScienceWorld, deterministic simulation dramatically outperforms LLM reasoning (Δ_full=+29.60), with **death avoidance as the dominant mechanism** (90.41% of the performance gap, measured by Δ decomposition). Episode-level label distribution: det-preferred 86 / internal-preferred 9 / no-preference 150 (out of 245 episodes). Non-death score deltas are small (Δ_nd=+2.84); 10/11 death-prone tasks show death-dominated performance gaps. One exception: find-non-living-thing (n=40, zero deaths, Δ=+9.58) demonstrates det advantage exists even without death risk. Pearson r=0.9698 (p=8.12e-07) between per-task death rate difference and Δ_full. The value of deterministic computation in interactive environments is concentrated in catastrophic failure prevention, not positive task guidance.\\n\\n**C2 (Episode-level counterfactual labeling as diagnostic methodology)**: Per-step oracle labeling degenerates in sparse-reward environments (98.2% tie rate on ScienceWorld). Episode-level counterfactual analysis — running complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies — overcomes this circularity and reveals the death-avoidance mechanism. The resulting labels train a lightweight router (Qwen3-1.7B) that serves as a **diagnostic probe** for LLM failure modes. [Hypothesis, pending plan-005]: the router may learn within-task-type early warning signals of catastrophic failure from early observations, beyond simple task-type classification.\\n\\n**D013 note**: C1 no longer claims \\\"selective > unconditional.\\\" Router training (plan-002/003) proceeds — if router ≈ always-det, that IS the finding; comparison with rule-based baseline (plan-011) quantifies whether learned routing adds value over keyword heuristics.\\n\\n## Positioning vs Tool-Use Literature (Dream-driven addition)\\n\\n**Critical gap identified by all 3 Dream tiers**: The core pipeline (counterfactual labels → SFT small classifier → selective invocation) is standard in tool-use learning. Must position against:\\n- **Toolformer** (Schick et al. 2024): Self-supervised tool-use learning via API call insertion. SimGate differs: hindsight labels from environment forking (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection).\\n- **ART** (Paranjape et al. 2023): Automated tool selection via LLM reasoning. SimGate: dedicated lightweight router, not LLM-as-router.\\n- **Chameleon** (Lu et al. 2024): LLM-as-planner routing to diverse tools. SimGate: single modality (deterministic computation), explicit small router.\\n- **ToolkenGPT** (Hao et al. 2024): Token-level tool triggers. SimGate: step-level routing with counterfactual labels.\\n\\n**Our differentiation**: (1) Episode-level counterfactual labeling — overcomes per-step oracle circularity in sparse-reward environments (98% tie rate), providing ground-truth episode outcomes rather than tie-break artifacts. (2) Empirical finding: death avoidance accounts for ~90% of routing signal — quantifies WHERE and WHY tool invocation helps (catastrophic failure prevention, not positive guidance). (3) Diagnostic framework — counterfactual analysis + router as probe reveals systematic LLM failure modes across task categories. (4) The contribution is the finding + methodology, not the router architecture — this distinguishes from \\\"we built a better tool selector\\\" papers.\\n\\n**Paper must include a dedicated Related Work section** (not just intro paragraphs). Minimum coverage: tool-use learning (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon), adaptive computation (CogRouter, ARES, Mixture-of-Depths), world model routing (ITP-R, Dyna-Think), agent frameworks (ReAct).\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: LLM agents hallucinate state transitions on rule-governed environments (temperature physics, chemical reactions), leading to catastrophic failures. ITP-R routes to an approximate LLM world model but underperforms pure internal reasoning (62.58 vs CogRouter 84.6 on ScienceWorld). ReTool/AgentMath learn when to invoke code interpreters but use implicit routing entangled with the backbone. Tool-use learning methods (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon) learn general tool selection but don't specialize for catastrophic failure prevention or use counterfactual trajectory labeling.\\n\\n- **Our framing**: We use episode-level counterfactual analysis to understand WHAT routing learns. Per-step oracle labeling degenerates (98% tie rate on ScienceWorld), so we run complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies, comparing episode-level outcomes. Key finding: ~90% of routing signal is death avoidance — deterministic computation's value is almost entirely concentrated in preventing catastrophic failures (-100 penalties). Non-death performance is approximately equal between modalities. A router trained on these labels becomes a diagnostic probe for LLM failure modes, but (per D013) is structurally limited to task-level risk classification under episode-level labels.\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"Episode-level counterfactual analysis across 11 ScienceWorld task types reveals that death avoidance accounts for ≥90% of routing signal between internal LLM reasoning and deterministic computation, with non-death score deltas near zero on 10/11 death-prone tasks. We propose this analysis as a diagnostic methodology for understanding when and why tool invocation helps LLM agents.\\\"\\n\\n## Paper Structure (4-page short paper)\\n\\n| Section | Pages | Content |\\n|---------|-------|---------|\\n| Abstract | 0.2 | Counterfactual analysis framing, death avoidance finding, headline numbers |\\n| Introduction | 0.8 | Problem (LLM catastrophic failures) + gap (per-step oracle degeneracy) + contribution (empirical finding + methodology) |\\n| Method | 1.0 | Episode-level counterfactual labeling (why per-step fails: 98% ties → episode-level solution); router training as downstream application; death decomposition analysis framework |\\n| Experiments | 1.5 | Death avoidance decomposition (core) + router vs baselines (always-det, rule-based, learned) + routing pattern analysis figure |\\n| Conclusion | 0.3 | Summary + limitations (episode-level granularity, single benchmark) + future (step-level labeling, MATH) |\\n| References | ~0.5 | Not counted in 4-page limit |\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Mitigations\\n\\n1. **\\\"Novelty is incremental — just SFT a small model to classify\\\"**\\n   - Mitigation: Contribution is the empirical finding (death avoidance mechanism + routing patterns) more than the architecture. Router-as-diagnostic-probe reveals systematic LLM failure modes. Explicit vs implicit ablation quantifies the gap.\\n\\n2. **\\\"Only one benchmark (ScienceWorld)\\\"**\\n   - Mitigation: Short paper format justifies focused evaluation. ScienceWorld uniquely tests rule-governed dynamics with catastrophic penalties. Discuss MATH/API extension as future work.\\n\\n3. **\\\"Comparison unfair — CogRouter uses RL (CoPO), you use SFT\\\"**\\n   - Mitigation: Our primary comparison is SimGate vs ablated baselines (always-internal, always-deterministic, random, heuristic) — all same training budget. CogRouter/ITP-R cited from papers for context.\\n\\n4. **\\\"Death avoidance is trivial — just always use deterministic\\\"**\\n   - Mitigation: We do NOT claim selective > unconditional deterministic. Our contribution is the empirical finding that death avoidance dominates routing signal (~90%), and the methodology that reveals this. Always-deterministic is a strong baseline — the interesting question is WHY (death avoidance), not WHETHER to route selectively. Plan-011 rule-based comparison + plan-012 death decomposition quantify this.\\n\\n5. **\\\"DAgger gap — SFT on pure-strategy trajectories may not transfer to mixed-strategy deployment\\\"**\\n   - Mitigation: Acknowledge explicitly (cite Ross et al. 2011). Plan C exacerbates this: router trains on always-internal/always-deterministic trajectories but deploys on mixed. Report train/test gap. If significant, discuss DAgger-style iterative relabeling as extension. Note: Plan C's episode-level labels avoid oracle circularity (no per-step tie-breaking), which is a methodological advantage even if distribution shift remains.\\n\\n6. **\\\"ScienceWorld's -100 penalty inflates gains\\\"** (Dream all 3 tiers)\\n   - Mitigation: Report gains WITH and WITHOUT death episodes separately. If non-death gains are small, honestly acknowledge that the primary value is catastrophic failure prevention — this IS our framing. Also report: what fraction of routing labels are genuine vs tie-break artifacts.\\n\\n7. **\\\"Missing tool-use literature — this is just Toolformer\\\"** (Dream all 3 tiers, CRITICAL)\\n   - Mitigation: Dedicated Related Work section. Position against Toolformer/ART/Chameleon. Differentiation: counterfactual trajectory labeling (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection), explicit modular router (not LLM-as-router).\\n\\n8. **\\\"Rule-based routing baseline missing\\\"** (Dream median + worst)\\n   - Mitigation: **D014 resolved — keyword routing structurally fails.** Two keyword lists tested: v1 (generic verbs incl. connect) → ≈always-det (85.8%); v2 (science-only: heat/boil/melt/freeze) → ≈always-internal (4.9%, near-zero hits). ScienceWorld actions use generic interaction verbs, not science keywords. Paper positions this as \\\"structural failure analysis\\\" — keyword heuristics fundamentally cannot capture routing signal in this environment, supporting the need for learned/observation-based approaches. D014: keywords v2 (science-only verbs), v1 had connect/disconnect degeneracy.\\n\\n## Venue Fit Risks\\n\\n- EMNLP LLM Agents track is a natural fit (tool use + planning + evaluation)\\n- Short paper format matches focused contribution scope\\n- Risk: Reviewer may expect ALFWorld evaluation (standard agent benchmark pair) — address in \\\"Scope & Future Work\\\" paragraph\\n- Risk: \\\"Death avoidance is the only signal\\\" may seem like a limited finding — mitigate by framing as \\\"this IS the insight\\\" (most routing literature assumes diverse routing benefits; we show it's dominated by one mechanism) + diagnostic methodology has value beyond ScienceWorld\\n- Risk: Router ≈ always-det ≈ rule-based keyword heuristic → novelty concern. **D014 update: keyword routing structurally fails on ScienceWorld** — v1 (generic verbs) ≈ always-det (85.8%), v2 (science keywords) ≈ always-internal (4.9%). # Paper Framing — simgate-modular-routing

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR short paper, 4 pages + references)
- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings
- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026 (11 days remaining)

## Core Insight

LLM agents on rule-governed environments face catastrophic failures from hallucinated state transitions. Deterministic external computation (environment simulators, code interpreters) eliminates these failures — but what exactly does routing learn? We introduce episode-level counterfactual analysis (per-step oracle labeling degenerates to 98% ties in sparse-reward settings) and discover that **death avoidance accounts for ~99% of routing signal** on ScienceWorld (Δ_full=+38.33, Δ_nd=+0.48, DAF=98.75%; Pearson r=0.9864, p<0.0001 across 30 task types / 249 episodes; source: plan-012, death_decomposition_report.json). Non-death performance is approximately equal between modalities (Δ_nd/Δ_full=1.3%). Five outlier tasks break the aggregate: 2 no-preference (find-non-living-thing DAF=-0.0, grow-plant DAF=null), 2 mid-range (find-living-thing DAF=89%, find-plant DAF=94%), 1 mixed signal (measure-melting-point-unknown DAF=59%, Δ_nd=+16.50). The contribution is the empirical finding (death avoidance dominance) + the diagnostic methodology (episode-level counterfactual labeling), not the router architecture itself.

## Core Claims (2 claims for short paper)

**C1 (Death avoidance dominates routing signal)**: On ScienceWorld, deterministic simulation dramatically outperforms LLM reasoning (Δ_full=+38.33), with **death avoidance as the dominant mechanism** (98.75% of the performance gap, measured by Δ decomposition; plan-012, 30 tasks / 249 eps). Episode-level label distribution: det-preferred 102 / internal-preferred 1 / no-preference 146 (out of 249 episodes). Of the 102 det-preferred labels, 93 (91.2%) arise from death asymmetry and 9 from non-death score comparison. Non-death score deltas are negligible (Δ_nd=+0.48, 1.3% of Δ_full); 25/30 task types show DAF ≥ 95%. Five outlier tasks: 2 no-preference (find-non-living-thing n=5, zero deaths, Δ=-6.80 internal-preferred; grow-plant n=20, zero deaths, Δ=0.00), 2 mid-range DAF (find-living-thing DAF=89%, find-plant DAF=94%), 1 mixed signal (measure-melting-point-unknown n=9, DAF=59%, Δ_nd=+16.50). Pearson r=0.9864 (p<0.0001) between per-task death rate difference and Δ_full across 30 task types. The value of deterministic computation in interactive environments is concentrated in catastrophic failure prevention, not positive task guidance.

**C2 (Episode-level counterfactual labeling as diagnostic methodology)**: Per-step oracle labeling degenerates in sparse-reward environments (98.2% tie rate on ScienceWorld). Episode-level counterfactual analysis — running complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies — overcomes this circularity and reveals the death-avoidance mechanism. The resulting labels train a lightweight router (Qwen3-1.7B) that serves as a **diagnostic probe** for LLM failure modes. [Hypothesis, pending plan-005]: the router may learn within-task-type early warning signals of catastrophic failure from early observations, beyond simple task-type classification.

**D013 note**: C1 no longer claims "selective > unconditional." Router training (plan-002/003) proceeds — if router ≈ always-det, that IS the finding; comparison with rule-based baseline (plan-011) quantifies whether learned routing adds value over keyword heuristics.

## Positioning vs Tool-Use Literature (Dream-driven addition)

**Critical gap identified by all 3 Dream tiers**: The core pipeline (counterfactual labels → SFT small classifier → selective invocation) is standard in tool-use learning. Must position against:
- **Toolformer** (Schick et al. 2024): Self-supervised tool-use learning via API call insertion. SimGate differs: hindsight labels from environment forking (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection).
- **ART** (Paranjape et al. 2023): Automated tool selection via LLM reasoning. SimGate: dedicated lightweight router, not LLM-as-router.
- **Chameleon** (Lu et al. 2024): LLM-as-planner routing to diverse tools. SimGate: single modality (deterministic computation), explicit small router.
- **ToolkenGPT** (Hao et al. 2024): Token-level tool triggers. SimGate: step-level routing with counterfactual labels.

**Our differentiation**: (1) Episode-level counterfactual labeling — overcomes per-step oracle circularity in sparse-reward environments (98% tie rate), providing ground-truth episode outcomes rather than tie-break artifacts. (2) Empirical finding: death avoidance accounts for ~99% of routing signal — quantifies WHERE and WHY tool invocation helps (catastrophic failure prevention, not positive guidance). (3) Diagnostic framework — counterfactual analysis + router as probe reveals systematic LLM failure modes across task categories. (4) The contribution is the finding + methodology, not the router architecture — this distinguishes from "we built a better tool selector" papers.

**Paper must include a dedicated Related Work section** (not just intro paragraphs). Minimum coverage: tool-use learning (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon), adaptive computation (CogRouter, ARES, Mixture-of-Depths), world model routing (ITP-R, Dyna-Think), agent frameworks (ReAct).

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: LLM agents hallucinate state transitions on rule-governed environments (temperature physics, chemical reactions), leading to catastrophic failures. ITP-R routes to an approximate LLM world model but underperforms pure internal reasoning (62.58 vs CogRouter 84.6 on ScienceWorld). ReTool/AgentMath learn when to invoke code interpreters but use implicit routing entangled with the backbone. Tool-use learning methods (Toolformer, ART, Chameleon) learn general tool selection but don't specialize for catastrophic failure prevention or use counterfactual trajectory labeling.

- **Our framing**: We use episode-level counterfactual analysis to understand WHAT routing learns. Per-step oracle labeling degenerates (98% tie rate on ScienceWorld), so we run complete episodes under pure-internal and pure-deterministic strategies, comparing episode-level outcomes. Key finding: ~99% of routing signal is death avoidance — deterministic computation's value is almost entirely concentrated in preventing catastrophic failures (-100 penalties). Non-death performance is approximately equal between modalities (Δ_nd=+0.48, 1.3% of Δ_full). A router trained on these labels becomes a diagnostic probe for LLM failure modes, but (per D013) is structurally limited to task-level risk classification under episode-level labels.

- **Headline result template**: "Episode-level counterfactual analysis across 30 ScienceWorld task types (249 episodes) reveals that death avoidance accounts for 98.75% of routing signal between internal LLM reasoning and deterministic computation (Δ_full=+38.33, Δ_nd=+0.48; r=0.9864, p<0.0001), with 25/30 tasks showing DAF ≥ 95%. We propose this analysis as a diagnostic methodology for understanding when and why tool invocation helps LLM agents."

## Paper Structure (4-page short paper)

| Section | Pages | Content |
|---------|-------|---------|
| Abstract | 0.2 | Counterfactual analysis framing, death avoidance finding, headline numbers |
| Introduction | 0.8 | Problem (LLM catastrophic failures) + gap (per-step oracle degeneracy) + contribution (empirical finding + methodology) |
| Method | 1.0 | Episode-level counterfactual labeling (why per-step fails: 98% ties → episode-level solution); router training as downstream application; death decomposition analysis framework |
| Experiments | 1.5 | Death avoidance decomposition (core) + router vs baselines (always-det, rule-based, learned) + routing pattern analysis figure |
| Conclusion | 0.3 | Summary + limitations (episode-level granularity, single benchmark) + future (step-level labeling, MATH) |
| References | ~0.5 | Not counted in 4-page limit |

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Mitigations

1. **"Novelty is incremental — just SFT a small model to classify"**
   - Mitigation: Contribution is the empirical finding (death avoidance mechanism + routing patterns) more than the architecture. Router-as-diagnostic-probe reveals systematic LLM failure modes. Explicit vs implicit ablation quantifies the gap.

2. **"Only one benchmark (ScienceWorld)"**
   - Mitigation: Short paper format justifies focused evaluation. ScienceWorld uniquely tests rule-governed dynamics with catastrophic penalties. Discuss MATH/API extension as future work.

3. **"Comparison unfair — CogRouter uses RL (CoPO), you use SFT"**
   - Mitigation: Our primary comparison is SimGate vs ablated baselines (always-internal, always-deterministic, random, heuristic) — all same training budget. CogRouter/ITP-R cited from papers for context.

4. **"Death avoidance is trivial — just always use deterministic"**
   - Mitigation: We do NOT claim selective > unconditional deterministic. Our contribution is the empirical finding that death avoidance dominates routing signal (~99%), and the methodology that reveals this. Always-deterministic is a strong baseline — the interesting question is WHY (death avoidance), not WHETHER to route selectively. Plan-011 rule-based comparison + plan-012 death decomposition quantify this.

5. **"DAgger gap — SFT on pure-strategy trajectories may not transfer to mixed-strategy deployment"**
   - Mitigation: Acknowledge explicitly (cite Ross et al. 2011). Plan C exacerbates this: router trains on always-internal/always-deterministic trajectories but deploys on mixed. Report train/test gap. If significant, discuss DAgger-style iterative relabeling as extension. Note: Plan C's episode-level labels avoid oracle circularity (no per-step tie-breaking), which is a methodological advantage even if distribution shift remains.

6. **"ScienceWorld's -100 penalty inflates gains"** (Dream all 3 tiers)
   - Mitigation: Report gains WITH and WITHOUT death episodes separately. If non-death gains are small, honestly acknowledge that the primary value is catastrophic failure prevention — this IS our framing. Also report: what fraction of routing labels are genuine vs tie-break artifacts.

7. **"Missing tool-use literature — this is just Toolformer"** (Dream all 3 tiers, CRITICAL)
   - Mitigation: Dedicated Related Work section. Position against Toolformer/ART/Chameleon. Differentiation: counterfactual trajectory labeling (not self-supervised), safety-aware framing (not general tool selection), explicit modular router (not LLM-as-router).

8. **"Rule-based routing baseline missing"** (Dream median + worst)
   - Mitigation: **D014 resolved — keyword routing structurally fails.** Two keyword lists tested: v1 (generic verbs incl. connect) → ≈always-det (85.8%); v2 (science-only: heat/boil/melt/freeze) → ≈always-internal (4.9%, near-zero hits). ScienceWorld actions use generic interaction verbs, not science keywords. Paper positions this as "structural failure analysis" — keyword heuristics fundamentally cannot capture routing signal in this environment, supporting the need for learned/observation-based approaches. D014: keywords v2 (science-only verbs), v1 had connect/disconnect degeneracy.

## Venue Fit Risks

- EMNLP LLM Agents track is a natural fit (tool use + planning + evaluation)
- Short paper format matches focused contribution scope
- Risk: Reviewer may expect ALFWorld evaluation (standard agent benchmark pair) — address in "Scope & Future Work" paragraph
- Risk: "Death avoidance is the only signal" may seem like a limited finding — mitigate by framing as "this IS the insight" (most routing literature assumes diverse routing benefits; we show it's dominated by one mechanism) + diagnostic methodology has value beyond ScienceWorld
- Risk: Router ≈ always-det ≈ rule-based keyword heuristic → novelty concern. **D014 update: keyword routing structurally fails on ScienceWorld** — v1 (generic verbs) ≈ always-det (85.8%), v2 (science keywords) ≈ always-internal (4.9%). ScienceWorld actions use generic interaction verbs (connect/move/pick up), not science-specific keywords, so no keyword list provides meaningful routing. This is a POSITIVE finding: positions keyword routing as "structural failure analysis" in the paper, strengthens case for learned routing or observation-based approaches.

## Key Differences from IDEA_BRIEF

1. **Scope narrowed**: IDEA_BRIEF proposed 3 tracks (ScienceWorld + ALFWorld + MATH). Short paper focuses on ScienceWorld only in main text; MATH as P1 extension; ALFWorld deferred.
2. **Framing shifted**: From "general routing to deterministic computation" to "safety-aware routing" based on MVP death avoidance finding.
3. **Claims reduced**: From 4 hypotheses (H1-H4) to 2 focused claims (C1-C2).
4. **"ANY form" softened**: Per Human Review Note #4, "across multiple forms" instead of "ANY form". Paper demonstrates principle on simulators; code interpreters discussed as extension.

## Data Provenance Note (added 2026-05-14)

**Authoritative data source**: `results/death_decomposition_report.json` on westb-13313, containing 30 tasks / 249 episodes full decomposition analysis. All quantitative claims in this document reference this single source. Historical intermediate analyses (11 tasks / 245 eps from plan-001b subset; 194 eps / 11 tasks from plan-003 baseline) are superseded and should NOT be cited.
